lines: וּבְתוֹךְ צַעֲקַת הֲמוֹנִים הוּא לוֹחֵשׁ לִי
לֹא תְּיַגַּע רֹאשִׁי מְבוּכָה אוֹ פַחַד
כִּי חַיַּי עִמּוֹ יְשִׁיבָה תְמִידִית שֶׁל־חֶבְרָה
יִשָּׁאֵר שְׁלוֹמִי שָׁלֵם, כִּי אֲדוֹן הָעוֹלָמִים
אֹמֵר: בְּטַח! הִנְנִי פֹּה, וְאַתָּה בְּחֵיקִי

review: The hymn is the beloved's repose: 1:1–4 is John 13:23 with Ps 32:8, 2:1–4 is Job 19:25 with 2 Cor 3:18 and Ps 16:11, 3:1–4 is Ps 102:26–27 with Isa 51:6 and Deut 33:27.

The three stanzas are all four long lines (14 syllables each), the print's `14,14,14,14`; the payload keeps the uniform long line rather than breaking it into couplets, because the hymn's effect is one continuous utterance.

3:4 אֹמֵר: בְּטַח! הִנְנִי פֹּה — the print sets the divine speech in quotation marks; the Hebrew uses the colon before direct speech per the glossary, and keeps the two imperatives separate so the line sounds like a voice and not a proverb.
2:4 uses שֶׁל־חֶבְרָה, taking the glossary's חֶבְרָה for the Arabic دَائِمَةٌ الْأُنْسِ, since 'company' is what the stanza has been describing and a loftier abstraction would lose the intimacy.
